title: Paul of the Cross (1694–1775)
hookLine: he founds the Passionists to remember Christ's passion

cards: Sewn on the chest of a black habit is a badge shaped like a heart, with a small cross rising from its top. Inside the heart, in Latin, the words: the Passion of Jesus Christ.

The men and women who wear it today are called Passionists. The badge goes back to an Italian man from a merchant family, who said he saw himself dressed this way in prayer, before any such habit existed.
He went on to preach in Italian villages, carrying a crucifix. His name in religion was Paul of the Cross.

teach.b: First, the call. As a young man, Paolo Danei felt drawn to a life of prayer and penance.

Tradition says that in prayer he saw the black habit and the sign of the Passion, and understood that he was to gather companions who would wear it. He went on retreat and wrote a rule for them. Second, the companions.
It was slow; few joined at first.

teach.h: SLOW YEARS, A BROTHER BESIDE HIM.
teach.b: His own brother, John Baptist, stayed beside him.
They lived simply on a mountain on the coast of Tuscany, praying and fasting, and the community grew, eventually with nuns as well. Third, the preaching.

Passionists went out to farm towns and villages to preach missions: days of sermons, confession and prayer. Paul preached holding a crucifix, telling people about Christ's sufferings as a sign of how much God loved them.
Passionists take a special vow to keep the memory of the Passion alive.
Fourth, the darkness. His letters show that for long years his own prayer felt dry and empty, as if God were far away. He kept preaching the cross while carrying one inside.
He died in Rome, and the Church canonized him.

In the letter to the Galatians, in the Douay-Rheims, Saint Paul the apostle writes: "But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." Paul of the Cross made that sentence his life's work.

how: Passionist priests, brothers and nuns wear the sign of the Passion on their habits and still preach parish missions and lead retreats centered on the cross, and Catholics often pray before a crucifix, especially on Fridays and in Lent.

games.q: Paul of the Cross — tap the pairs.

s: Paul of the Cross felt close to God every day of his life
his letters show long years when his prayer felt dry and God seemed far away.
Passionists take a special vow to keep the memory of Christ's passion alive
it's at the center of their life and preaching.
the community grew quickly from the start
it was slow; few joined at first, and his brother stayed beside him.

games.q: you're Paul. your prayer has felt empty for years, and tomorrow you're to preach a mission in a village. what do you do?
o: cancel until you feel close to God again.
go, crucifix in hand, and preach the love you can't feel right now.
hand the mission to someone else for good.
games.why: he kept preaching the cross while carrying a darkness of his own, as his letters show.

practice: Hold a crucifix or a cross if one is nearby, or look at a picture of one, and don't study it; just stay with it, the way Paul stayed through his dry years.
Bring to mind one person who is suffering, and let the cross and that person rest together; Paul of the Cross believed love could be seen here.
If you pray, stay there with Christ in silence and bring that person with you; if you don't, let the image show you what someone gave for others.

wordCard.voice: Paolo Danei. The birth name of Paul of the Cross, who saw himself in prayer wearing a black habit with the sign of the Passion, before it existed.

orig.note: Latin: the Passion of Jesus Christ, the words on the Passionist badge. XPI abbreviates Christi.

carryVoice: Your line: remember the passion. He preached the cross through years when his own prayer felt empty. Rest well.
